mostWorthwhile.text: The population example was most worthwhile: its arithmetic showed why unequal reproduction changes variant frequencies and why scarcity alone cannot predict which variant increases.

leastWorthwhile.text: The geological-time connection was useful but felt somewhat predictable: more time permits accumulated change without proving selection.

surprise.text: I was surprised that Darwin also accepted inherited effects of use and disuse, rather than the accounts being wholly exclusive.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the geological-time combination was the only offered action rather than a meaningful choice among alternatives.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the unresolved inheritance problem is addressed; this chapter made clear that selection assumes persistent variants without explaining their transmission.
